svg.title: architect-os: what is ready, and where what comes next will join
svg.desc: The architecture of architect-os in one image, in five parts. Ready marks components implemented in this version. Next marks planned work or pending integration beside the brick it will join. 1. The native gateway authenticates each client on loopback and routes its calls to modules and task workers. The gateway starts the data process and the model broker on standard input and output. Only data holds the database URL. Data keeps the memories, the usage, the tasks and, in its steps tables, the state of a Step, through typed operations only. Only the model broker holds the API key. A module calls back with its call ID. A worker can reach only the broker and uses a token scoped to its task. 2. Define reads a validated prd-gen handoff over MCP from the bundle the operator pinned by its SHA-256. Optional ticket estimates and prerequisites reach the approved Step and its host record. The named Spec producer still needs both versioned projections. The admitted planning host can drive a pinned Spec bundle through drafting and independent review and resume from its private journal. Plan accepts the verified Spec proposal or a draft from Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity. It can also import a completed Antigravity exchange. Plan previews one Step. A plain proposal can be materialized with local approval. The independently reviewed Spec projection stops at preview. Step verifies a separate host receipt for its inputs, target tree, launcher, independent reviews and prompt specimens. The host verifies scout citations against repository lines before including them in the Builder brief. The orchestration loop takes a brief, those verified facts, a build session, checks without a model, the replay of the host, reviews that cannot write the worktree and give a status for every approved acceptance criterion, the gate, and a delivery command written to push the same commit to the work branch and then to main, while main now takes pull requests only; after a refusal, the orchestrator writes a new brief; the host writes steps/<name>/ into the worktree and commits each pass on its work branch, refused ones included, so that the next pass starts clean from that commit and builds on it. Deliver checks Linux and macOS for the candidate commit, verifies the job count and execution IDs for each numbered attempt, and reads every attempt for planned mutation lanes. Each planned family reserves its prefix across the configuration; fixed producers may be shared explicitly. The Linux judge checks the job lists of all attempts and the artifact list of its run before downloading. Next, the delivery opens a pull request on the target repository, its body rendered from the record of the Step. Next in the loop: three explorations before Plan and the remaining human gates; an issuer of the production receipt that Step requires; and a measure of the duration of the suite, alone and under contention. Step builds through one typed Builder port with two adapters: Claude Code under SRT, and the pinned Codex 0.170.0 client in a Docker SBX Linux VM for Astra and Sol. On macOS, the real production entry ran both Steps with the real client under an unprivileged user. The native tool wrote the file in the worktree, the SRT checker read it, and the host published a record with the model, effort, client digest and terminal usage. The test processes simulated the identity service and the model responses, and the Claude review was a recorded stream. The subscription is installed once and kept in the host credential store between Steps. The macOS Keychain was exercised by two processes, with one renewal for two concurrent consumers, and a Step without an account stopped with SBX_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED. The VM reaches the Step proxy on the host and the npm registry. A second listening port received nothing and a request outside the route was refused. The open trial is a production Step whose patch the real model chooses on the subscription. The Linux Secret Service store is not yet verified and the monetary cost is unknown. Gemini reviews through the native Google agent outside SBX. The historical Antigravity probe stopped at session creation. Nine earlier single-request trials ran the text-only bench protocol; six provider completions reported 402 tokens. 3. The isolation diagram places the host beside two separate runtimes. SRT isolates production Step sessions and the gateway’s modules and workers in OS processes under five profiles. Docker SBX creates a Linux VM for the native Builder. Its unprivileged native client posts to the Step proxy on the host over HTTP and reaches the npm registry; any other port or destination is refused. The host keeps the subscription in its OS credential store between Steps, renews it and verifies the account. The host meters terminal usage and verifies VM removal. The Builder writes the worktree while the host controls Git metadata. Host Git sources attributes from the empty tree. The fingerprint, Gate and Deliver check for visible nested Git markers before untracked discovery. The Gate lease and Deliver also compare checkout bytes with the commit. Fingerprint, Gate and Deliver pass Git pathnames to the guard as bytes, and Host Git takes one closed option set. The authentication proxy on the host gives the Claude session a scoped token so the credential stays on the host throughout the session. The required ./aos entry checks the marked runtime root and the available space on the root and home filesystems before npm, then records admission in the new run directory. Repository automation uses this entry. All five profiles use private session directories. The host retains Step results and journals under the root and writes raw streams to the run temporary directory. Gate locks each physical checkout, writes to its run reports directory, and retains the checked Linux receipt for Deliver. A canary under the same profile must fail before each command. What each profile opens is the generated image isolation-profiles.svg, held equal to the five profile files by the gate. 4. Five checks before the gate, then the host gate and npm run deliver. In CI, two entry workflows with the same jobs serve pull requests and pushes; a new commit of a pull request cancels the run of the commit it supersedes, and a push run is never cancelled that way. Linux splits the full scenario suite into two shards and checks mutants in one to sixteen lanes planned from the commit, with independent replay, and the judge derives the plan again. On the host the gate judges the merge GitHub builds and refuses a destination that is missing, in conflict or not integrated; it walks source directories on disk and refuses links, invalid UTF-8 and Stryker directives without their justified form. The hosted judge uses its read token to retrieve the parent count and list the jobs and artifacts, and checks those lists before it fetches any archive. Next, Deliver binds the run it reads to its workflow, the push event, the trial branch and the SHA together. The three Claude workflows of CI run on ubuntu-24.04: each installs its managed settings and proves bubblewrap before the action, which starts only when both steps succeeded. Next: the subscription token, today a repository secret that a same-repository pull request rewriting a workflow receives, given only to the files of main. The Claude review runs the action v1.0.290 in its official mode, without a shell, under a hook that guards its comments, and closes its tracking comment with its verdict; the security review is advisory, and a job without a model posts its findings. main takes pull requests only: its ruleset requires the checks gate-linux and gate-macos with no bypass actor, and the resolver merges a pull request when its gate is green and the Claude review of the same head approves. Fresh inputs are a check applied before delivery, played by hand; making them a phase of the Step is next. macOS runs the sandbox scenarios. 5. The evidence desk verifies each DOI at doi.org and matches normalized passages in the supplied full text; the watch of Anthropic compares the public sources the platform relies on with a committed register. The register names 31 sources, 25 of them pages.

Each profile has private session folders and the same denied read paths.
Its file defines writes, network destinations and credentials. The gateway
starts one process per module and a fresh worker for each task run.
Before each command, the same profile must deny a sibling secret and
an unlisted loopback port. A failed canary stops the command. The suite
tests eight attacks per profile and three Builder writes to steps/.

The gate (1a): npm run gate on the host, then CI on Linux and macOS
Two entries: gate.yml for pull requests, where a new commit cancels the superseded run, and gate-push.yml for

g.aria-label: The Claude workflows of CI · ready, with the subscription token · next
g.text: The Claude workflows of CI: claude.yml, claude-review.yml, claude-security-review.yml
On ubuntu-24.04, each job installs its managed settings, then proves bubblewrap: signed Ubuntu packages, the AppArmor
restriction on user namespaces lowered, one namespace created. The action starts only when both steps succeeded, and
Claude Code scrubs the environment of its subprocesses. Every job of every workflow names its image, never a -latest label.
claude-review runs action v1.0.290 in its official mode, without a shell; a comment-guard hook refuses mentions, a misplaced
verdict and credentials, and the verdict closes its tracking comment. The security review is advisory; a job without a model posts it.
The subscription token is a repository secret: a same-repository pull request that rewrites a workflow receives it. Next: files of main only.

g.aria-label: main takes pull requests only · ready
g.text: main takes pull requests only: docs/design/ruleset-main.json and pipeline-after-merge.yml
The ruleset requires a pull request and the checks gate-linux and gate-macos, with no bypass actor. The resolver merges a pull
request when the gate of its head is green and the Claude review of that head approves; the security review advises only.
